criteria.semantics:
A native

in its place on the page, its text the status's content. It is not a live region: the page has one, the shell's #status, which says what changed; an in-place status is read where it stands.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.

criteria.name: None: a status is read in place, not named.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the status grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the status wrap in its place, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement:
The face emits a native

element.
The paragraph's text is the status's content.
The status is quiet: no aria-live and no status, alert or log role, so only the shell's #status announces.
A status is not a control: nothing in it is a stop in the tab order.
WHEN I read the page with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR the status in its place in the reading order.
WHEN the status changes after something I did I HEAR it said once, by the shell's #status, and never twice.

criteria.semantics: The status's content as text in fg on bg, in its place in the window. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Status node, polite, so a change is said once (AXApplicationStatus on macOS, a Text control with LiveSetting Polite on Windows, a status bar or live region on AT-SPI).

keyboard.outcome: Pass the status by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

criteria.name: None: a status is read in place.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the status grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the status drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the status at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the status drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the status whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A status adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the status's content as text in its place, in words, not only in color.
WHEN the status changes with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) running I HEAR the new status said once, without moving the focus.

announce.api: AXGroup with AXSubrole AXApplicationStatus, polite (AccessKit Role::Status, Live::Polite).
ControlType Text with LiveSetting Polite, raising LiveRegionChanged on a change.
ATSPI_ROLE_STATUS_BAR with the live attribute polite, emitting a text change.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
